statement: Explicit valuation coordinates. There is an isomorphism of topological abelian groups \[ \widehat{\Q^\times}\simeq \{\pm1\}\times \left\{(a_q)_q\in\prod_q\widehat{\Z}: \text{for every }n,\ a_q\in n\widehat{\Z} \text{ for all but finitely many }q\right\}. \] It is induced by the sign and the prime valuations. The group on the right is given the inverse-limit topology: a basic neighbourhood of zero requires every coordinate, simultaneously, to vanish modulo a fixed $n$. This specifies the topology used in the isomorphism. A class is locally represented by an element of $\Q_p^\times$ exactly when its $p$-valuation belongs to $\Z\subset\widehat{\Z}$. It is represented by a rational number exactly when all these valuations are integers and only finitely many are nonzero.

statement: The twenty-four central twists and the exact local matching map. Use the actual class-two quotient $E_2=H(\widehat\Z)\rtimes G_\Q$ and its coordinates from A.38. Thus this fiber contains exactly twenty-four classes. The localization homomorphism on these central twists is \[ \operatorname{loc}:\Z/24\longrightarrow \prod_{q<\infty}H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{\Q_q},\widehat\Z(2)), \qquad k\longmapsto(\operatorname{res}_q(k\eta))_q. \tag{A.40.3} \] It is injective. Its composite with the two coordinate projections at $(q,\ell)=(2,3),(3,2)$ is the isomorphism \[ \begin{split} \Z/24&\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \Z_3/3\Z_3\oplus\Z_2/8\Z_2,\\ k&\longmapsto(k/8\bmod3,\ k/3\bmod8). \end{split} \tag{A.40.4} \] For each ordinary local coordinate $x_q$ of $(A,B)$, the actual local point section determines a local comparison class $\delta_q$ relative to any chosen global class-two lift, as constructed in the proof. The subset of global lift classes agreeing with all these local point-section classes is exactly \[ \bigl\{s+k\eta:\ k\in\Z/24, \ (\delta_q)_q=\operatorname{loc}(k)\bigr\}. \tag{A.40.5} \] Consequently this subset has at most one element. For every $(A,B)\in\mathcal G$, there is a unique global class-two lift whose two central comparison coordinates in (A.40.4) agree with the local points at $2$ and $3$. statement: The weight-three test on the twenty-four integral lifts. Put $E_3=E_U/\Gamma_4\Pi$, where $\Gamma_4\Pi=\overline{[\Pi,\Gamma_3\Pi]}$. With the generators and tangent of A.38, set \[ C=[x,y],\qquad D=[C,x],\qquad F=[C,y]. \] The kernel of $E_3\to E_2$ is $\widehat\Z(3)D\oplus\widehat\Z(3)F$. Set $\varepsilon=(\chi-1)/2$ and $\eta=(\chi^2-1)/24$. Its components are represented by the continuous two-cocycles \[ \begin{split} W_D&=-(a+\varepsilon)\cup h-\binom a2\cup b,\\ W_F&=(b+\varepsilon)\cup(ab-h)+\binom b2\cup a-\eta\cup b. \end{split} \tag{A.43.1} \] Here $ab$ and $\binom a2$ are pointwise one-cochains with coefficient weight two. In particular all the expressions are integral, including at two. The twenty-four classes in A.40 have the exact obstruction values \[ \mathbf o_3(s+k\eta)=\mathbf o_3(s) -k\bigl((A+\kappa(-1))\cup[\eta], (B+\kappa(-1))\cup[\eta]\bigr), \qquad k\in\Z/24. \tag{A.43.2} \] Let $(A,B)\in\mathcal G$, with ordinary coordinates $x_q$, and let $\delta_q$ be its comparison class from (A.40.16). For $q\ne\ell$ denote the Frobenius coordinate of its $\ell$-part by \[ d_{q,\ell}\in\Z_\ell/(q^2-1)\Z_\ell =H^1(G_{\Q_q},\Z_\ell(2)). \] Under the standard tame-residue isomorphism \[ \rho_{q,\ell}:H^2(G_{\Q_q},\Z_\ell(3)) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Z_\ell/(q^2-1)\Z_\ell, \tag{A.43.3} \] the two localized weight-three obstructions are exactly \[ \rho_{q,\ell}\bigl(\mathbf o_3(s)|_{G_{\Q_q}}\bigr) =\bigl(-v_q(x_q)d_{q,\ell}, -v_q(1-x_q)d_{q,\ell}\bigr). \tag{A.43.4} \] Thus their common zero locus at this place is the annihilator of the two indicated valuation integers in the displayed finite cyclic module. Write $\mathscr L_i(A,B)$ for the geometric conjugacy classes of $E_i$-sections with abelian image $(A,B)$, and $s_*$ for the distinguished class of A.40. On the ordinary locus with \[ (v_2(x_2),v_2(1-x_2))=(0,1),\qquad (v_3(x_3),v_3(1-x_3))=(1,0), \tag{A.43.5} \] the actual projection of section sets satisfies \[ \operatorname{im}\bigl(\mathscr L_3(A,B)\longrightarrow \mathscr L_2(A,B)\bigr)\subseteq\{s_*\}. \tag{A.43.6} \] For the rational pair $(A,B)=(\kappa(3),\kappa(-2))$, this image is exactly the class-two point-section class at $3$.

statement: Infinite-support ghosts survive every fixed finite geometric quotient with full abelianization. Let $N$ be a closed normal subgroup of $E_U$ contained in $\Pi$, and suppose $Q=\Pi/N$ is finite. Write \[ E_Q=E_U/N,\quad E_{Q^{\rm ab}}=E_Q/[Q,Q],\quad E_1=E_U/\Gamma_2\Pi. \] The natural map is an isomorphism of profinite extensions of $G_\Q$, \[ E_U/(N\cap\Gamma_2\Pi) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } E_Q\mathop{\times}_{E_{Q^{\rm ab}}}E_1. \tag{A.51.1} \] For every such $Q$, the extension on the left has a continuous section whose full abelian Kummer coordinates form an ordinary infinite-support ghost of the form A.44. Its image in $E_Q$ is the image of the rational point section at $3$. For perfect $Q$, every ordinary ghost admits a section of this extension with that prescribed $E_Q$ image. These sections are excluded from the rational-point and cuspidal images by their full abelian coordinates. Thus no single finite geometric quotient, adjoined to the full abelianization in the exact sense (A.51.1), eliminates all ordinary infinite-support ghosts. This includes any fixed finite modular quotient with geometric group $A_4,(\Z/2)^2,A_5$ or $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbf F_7)$. The assertion prescribes a global quotient section; matching its finite-quotient localizations to the points $x_p$ is an additional requirement.

statement: Exact level-three, four, five and seven maps. Put $k=\bar\Q$. The projective geometric quotients of the Legendre monodromy at levels $N=3,4,5,7$, and the smooth compactifications of their connected covers of $U_k$, are as follows: \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c} N&\text{linear image}&\text{projective image }Q_N &\text{compactification}&\text{genus}\\ \hline 3&\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf F_3)&A_4&X(6)_k&1\\ 4& (\Z/2)^2&(\Z/2)^2&X(4)_k&0\\ 5&\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf F_5)&A_5&X(10)_k&13\\ 7&\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf F_7)& \operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbf F_7)&X(14)_k&49. \end{array} \tag{A.53.1} \] Here $X(N)$ has its usual symplectic modular meaning over a field containing the relevant roots of unity. The geometric assertions in the table do not assert that every arithmetic twist has a rational point or is isomorphic over $\Q$ to that chosen modular model. The group $S_4\simeq\operatorname{SL}_2(\Z/4)/\{\pm I\}$ belongs to $X(4)\to X(1)$ over the $j$-line. The component obtained after pullback along $X(2)\to X(1)$ has group \[ \ker\bigl(S_4\longrightarrow S_3\bigr)=(\Z/2)^2. \tag{A.53.2} \] At odd $N$ in the table the connected pullback is $X(2N)$. In particular, the genus-zero curves $X(3),X(5)$ and the genus-three curve $X(7)$ in L10 are the curves before this pullback. For each $N$ let \[ N_N=\ker\bigl(\Pi\xrightarrow{\rho_{\rm Leg,N}} \operatorname{GL}_2(\Z/N)\longrightarrow \operatorname{PGL}_2(\Z/N)\bigr). \tag{A.53.3} \] This is a closed normal subgroup of $E_U$, and the section in the question has the actual quotient section \[ G_\Q\xrightarrow{s}E_U\longrightarrow E_U/N_N, \qquad \Pi/N_N=Q_N. \tag{A.53.4} \] Thus A.51 applies with precisely the four groups in (A.53.1). For $N=5,7$ these groups are perfect. For $N=4$ the quotient already factors through the full geometric abelianization; adjoining it to that abelianization adds no further quotient information.

statement: A general recognition criterion with one coordinate supported at two. Let $m\ge5$ be odd, and let \[ \lambda_0=2^m\quad\hbox{or}\quad\lambda_0=1+2^m. \] Write $M=2^m-1$ in the first case and $M=2^m+1$ in the second. Let $s$ be a noncuspidal Selmer section whose full integral Legendre representation is conjugate to that of the point $\lambda_0$ by an element of the geometric closure $H$ in A.17. Every prime $p\mid M$ at which $s_p$ is cuspidal satisfies \[ p\nmid(m-4),\qquad \left(\frac{4-m}{p}\right)=1. \tag{A.54.1} \] Consequently, when no prime divisor of $M$ satisfies (A.54.1), $s$ is precisely the point section $s_{\lambda_0}$. In particular, the conclusion holds for $\lambda_0=33$: $M=33=3\cdot11$ and $4-m=-1$ is a nonsquare modulo both prime divisors. This example settles its exact A7 recognition question. The proof uses the determinant-one hypothesis on the conjugator; it does not assert this conclusion for every unrestricted integral $\operatorname{GL}_2$-intertwiner.

statement: The dual obstruction to correction using completely split auxiliary primes. Let $N\ge2$, let $M_N=\Z/N(2)$, and identify its Cartier dual by the evaluation pairing \[ M_N^D=\operatorname{Hom}(M_N,\mu_N)=\Z/N(-1),\qquad M_N\otimes M_N^D\longrightarrow\mu_N. \tag{A.55.1} \] Let $K/\Q$ be finite Galois containing $\mu_N$, let $S$ contain the infinite place, the primes dividing $N$, and the primes ramified in $K$, and let $T$ be the set of finite primes outside $S$ which split completely in $K$. Write $H^1_{S\cup T}(\Q,M_N)$ for the union of $H^1(G_{\Q,S\cup T_0},M_N)$ over finite $T_0\subset T$. Then \[ \begin{aligned} &\operatorname{im}\left(H^1_{S\cup T}(\Q,M_N) \longrightarrow\prod_{v\in S}H^1(\Q_v,M_N)\right) \\ &\qquad=\left(\operatorname{res}_S H^1(\operatorname{Gal}(K/\Q),M_N^D)\right)^\perp. \end{aligned} \tag{A.55.2} \] Here the annihilator is taken under the actual pairing \[ ((z_v),\xi)\longmapsto \sum_{v\in S}\operatorname{inv}_v (z_v\cup\operatorname{res}_v\xi) \quad\hbox{in }\Q/\Z. \tag{A.55.3} \] There is a concrete order-sixteen character in this dual group. Suppose $N=2^r$ with $r\ge4$, take $c=2v^{24}\in\Q^\times$, and use compatible Kummer coordinates $b=\kappa_N(c)\in Z^1(G_\Q,\Z/N(1))$. For $g\in G_\Q$ write \[ \chi(g)\bmod16=(-1)^{e(g)}5^{L(g)},\quad L(g)\in\Z/4, \qquad \beta(g)=\frac{\chi(g)^2-1}{8}\bmod2. \tag{A.55.4} \] The function $\binom{L}{2}\bmod2$ is well defined on $\Z/4$. Then \[ \zeta_N(g)=\frac N{16}b(g)+\frac N2\binom{L(g)}2 \quad\hbox{in }\Z/N(-1) \tag{A.55.5} \] is a continuous one-cocycle. Its cohomology class has exact order $16$ and factors through \[ K_c=\Q(\mu_N,c^{1/N}). \tag{A.55.6} \] Moreover, \[ 2\zeta_N=\frac N8\kappa_N(c),\qquad 8\zeta_N=\frac N2\beta \quad\hbox{as actual cocycles}. \tag{A.55.7} \] The first expression on the right is viewed in weight $-1$ by the equivariant coefficient map $\Z/N(1)\to\Z/N(-1)$, $u\mapsto(N/8)u$. For an explicit failed correction problem, take \[ c=2\cdot73^{24},\qquad S=\{2,73,\infty\}, \qquad K=K_c. \tag{A.55.8} \] At $73$ let $z_{73}$ be the unramified class in $H^1(\Q_{73},M_N)$ with arithmetic Frobenius value $1$, and prescribe $z_2=z_\infty=0$. This tuple is not in the image in (A.55.2), for every $r\ge4$. There is also an exact constraint on retaining the integral class-two section. For every prime $\ell$ and $a\ge1$, the coefficient connecting map gives the exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow \frac{H^1_{\rm cts}(G_\Q,\Z_\ell(2))}{\ell^a} \longrightarrow H^1(G_\Q,\Z/\ell^a(2)) \xrightarrow{\ \partial\ } H^2_{\rm cts}(G_\Q,\Z_\ell(2))[\ell^a] \longrightarrow0. \tag{A.55.9} \] A finite central correction $z$ of a fixed integral class-two lift is the reduction of an integral central correction exactly when $\partial z=0$. This is equivalent to $z$ being unramified outside $\ell$, with the additional condition $\operatorname{res}_\infty z=0$ when $\ell=2$. Thus the allowable integral corrections are precisely the reductions of the groups computed in A.40. Once its two cross-prime normalizations are imposed, none of their nonzero classes survives at modulus divisible by $24$.

statement: Exact abelian image of the full congruence kernel. Let $H$ be the full geometric Legendre image in A.17, and put \[ C=\ker(\Pi\longrightarrow H),\qquad T=\Pi^{\rm ab}=\widehat\Z(1)^2. \] All derived subgroups in this statement are closed derived subgroups. There is an isomorphism of finite $G_\Q$-modules \[ H^{\rm ab}\simeq (\Z/8(1))^2\oplus\Z/3(1), \tag{A.56.1} \] under which the map induced by the two Kummer coordinates is \[ T\longrightarrow H^{\rm ab},\qquad (a,b)\longmapsto(a\bmod8, b\bmod8, a+b\bmod3). \tag{A.56.2} \] In particular, the image of $C$ in $T$ is exactly the open subgroup \[ K=\{(a,b):a\equiv b\equiv0\pmod8,\quad a+b\equiv0\pmod3\}. \tag{A.56.3} \] Set $E_H=E_U/C$, $E_{H^{\rm ab}}=E_H/[H,H]$, and $E_1=E_U/\Gamma_2\Pi$. The natural map is an isomorphism of profinite extensions, \[ E_U/(C\cap\Gamma_2\Pi) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } E_H\mathop{\times}_{E_{H^{\rm ab}}}E_1. \tag{A.56.4} \] Fix a rational point $b_0\in U(\Q)$. Given completed Kummer classes $(A,B)$, a section of (A.56.4) with these abelian classes and with its $E_H$ image equal to the point section at $b_0$ exists exactly when \[ \begin{split} A&\equiv b_0\pmod{(\widehat{\Q^\times})^8},\\ B&\equiv1-b_0\pmod{(\widehat{\Q^\times})^8},\\ AB&\equiv b_0(1-b_0)\pmod{(\widehat{\Q^\times})^3}. \end{split} \tag{A.56.5} \] These expressions mean equality under the canonical projections to $\Q^\times/(\Q^\times)^8$ and $\Q^\times/(\Q^\times)^3$, respectively. The ordinary infinite-support ghosts of A.44 satisfy (A.56.5) for $b_0=3$. They therefore define global sections of this quotient with the entire congruence representation of the honest point $3$, including its determinant and its integral pairings. At every fresh support prime in the construction, these quotient sections fail the local Legendre comparison with their prescribed ordinary point. They are therefore not images of Selmer sections of $E_U$. The exact full-section recognition question in A7 is not decided by this quotient construction.

statement: Joint fibre characters and their two-primary bound. Let $4\mid n$, let $D_1,\ldots,D_k\in\Q^\times$, and let \[ \mathcal E=\Q[Z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,Z_k^{\pm1}] /(Z_i^n-D_i:1\le i\le k). \tag{A.57.1} \] This is a finite etale algebra. The finite-order abelian characters of $G_\Q$ that vanish on the absolute Galois group of every field factor of $\mathcal E$ have the following exact finite description. Write \[ D_i=(-1)^{\delta_i}\prod_{P\in\mathcal P}P^{w_{iP}}, \quad \delta_i\in\{0,1\},\qquad F=\Q(\mu_{2n},\sqrt P:P\in\mathcal P),\qquad \Gamma=\operatorname{Gal}(F/\Q). \tag{A.57.2} \] For $\sigma\in\Gamma$ define $u_\sigma\in(\Z/2n)^\times$ and $\epsilon_P(\sigma)\in\Z/2$ by \[ \sigma(\zeta_{2n})=\zeta_{2n}^{u_\sigma}, \qquad \sigma(\sqrt P)=(-1)^{\epsilon_P(\sigma)}\sqrt P. \] Let $\mathcal A\subset\Gamma$ consist of the $\sigma$ for which there are $k_P\in\Z/n$ and $e_i\in\Z/n$ satisfying \[ \begin{split} k_P&\equiv\epsilon_P(\sigma)\pmod2,\\ (u_\sigma-1)(\delta_i+2e_i) +2\sum_Pw_{iP}k_P&\equiv0\pmod {2n} \quad(1\le i\le k). \end{split} \tag{A.57.3} \] Put $H=\langle\mathcal A\rangle\subset\Gamma$. Then the required character group is exactly \[ \operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma/H,\Q/\Z). \tag{A.57.4} \] Equivalently, the largest abelian field contained in every field factor of (A.57.1) is $B=F^H$. Writing $n=2^r v$ with $v$ odd, one has the sharper bound \[ B\subset \Q(\sqrt P:P\in\mathcal P)\,\Q(\mu_{2^{r+1}}). \tag{A.57.5} \] In particular every character in (A.57.4) has order a power of two. Formula (A.57.3), or the equivalent divisibility test below, determines the remaining cyclotomic and quadratic relations; complete splitting in the whole radical splitting field imposes more conditions than (A.57.4).

statement: An integral valuation locus in the image of the full class-three section map. Let $\mathcal V_3$ be the set of ordinary completed unit-equation pairs $(A,B)$ with the following valuation data. At $2$ and $3$, respectively, the two valuations are \[ (v_2(A),v_2(B))=(0,1),\qquad (v_3(A),v_3(B))=(1,0). \tag{A.58.1} \] For each prime $q>3$, the two valuations are one of \[ (0,0),\quad(24e_q(q^2-1),0),\quad(0,24e_q(q^2-1)),\quad (-24e_q(q^2-1),-24e_q(q^2-1)), \tag{A.58.2} \] where $e_q$ is a nonnegative integer, and the family $(e_q)_{q>3}$ converges to zero in $\widehat\Z$: for every positive integer $N$, only finitely many $e_q$ are nonzero modulo $N$. Thus the composite of (A.58.3) with abelianization has image containing $\mathcal V_3$, with the intermediate class-two class uniquely specified.

statement: Ordinary ghosts with both higher-weight valuation factors. For every positive integer $C$ divisible by $24$ there is an infinite-support ordinary completed unit-equation pair with the following explicit valuation pattern. statement: A nonconstant joint fibre character and an obstructed new coordinate. Put \[ c_1=0,\quad c_2=1,\quad c_3=-\frac{9563}{59024}, \qquad R=\frac1{17},\qquad c=-\frac{11}{68}, \qquad a_i=R-c_i. \tag{A.69.1} \] Let $C$ be the smooth projective compactification of the Kummer cover with affine equations \[ T-c_i=a_iX_i^4\qquad(1\le i\le3). \tag{A.69.2} \] It has the rational point $P_0=(R,1,1,1)$ and a point $P_2\in C(\Q_2)$ with \[ T(P_2)=\frac{16}{17},\qquad X_1(P_2)=2, \quad X_2(P_2)=\frac12, \quad X_3(P_2)^4=\frac{4341}{869}. \tag{A.69.3} \] Every field factor of the fibre of (A.69.2) at $T=c$ contains $\Q(\mu_8)$. statement: Nonconstant joint fibre characters at every exponent divisible by four. The even cyclotomic character \[ \chi_r:\operatorname{Gal}(\Q(\mu_{2^{r+1}})/\Q) \longrightarrow\Q/\Z, \qquad \chi_r(-1)=0,\quad\chi_r(5)=\frac1h, \tag{A.73.2} \] gives a class on the smooth projective model $C$, \[ \mathcal A_n= \left(\frac{T-c}{-c},\chi_r\right)\in\operatorname{Br}C, \qquad \mathcal A_n(P_0)=0, \qquad \operatorname{inv}_2\mathcal A_n(P_2)=\frac12. \tag{A.73.3} \] The notation $(f,\chi_r)$ denotes the cyclic-algebra class, with the convention $\operatorname{inv}_2(f,\chi_r) =\chi_r(\operatorname{rec}_2(f))$. statement: A multiplier-independent quadratic obstruction recognizes the parameter thirty-four. Let $\lambda\in2\Z\setminus\{0\}$, put $k=v_2(\lambda)$, and write \[ |1-\lambda|=\prod_{q\in Q}q^{e_q}. \tag{A.82.1} \] Let $P$ be the odd primes dividing $\lambda$, together with two when $k\ge5$. statement: A necessary and sufficient finite-character test. Let $4\mid n$ and let the old cover $C$ and new puncture $c$ be as in (A.83.1)--(A.83.2), without the squareclass restriction of A.83. Let $B_c$ be the common abelian fibre field computed by A.57 for \[ \mathcal E_c=\Q[Z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,Z_k^{\pm1}] /(Z_i^n-(c-c_i)/a_i). \tag{A.85.1} \] Choose a finite set $S$ containing the ramified primes of its splitting field, the coefficient, denominator and difference primes specified in A.83, and all primes up to the uniform augmented-cover bound (A.83.5). For every $v\in S\cup\{\infty\}$ prescribe a point $P_v\in C(\Q_v)$ with $T(P_v)\ne c$. Define the finite character obstruction by the actual local reciprocity maps: \[ \mathfrak o_c((P_v))= \prod_{v\in S\cup\{\infty\}} \operatorname{rec}_v(T(P_v)-c)\bigm|_{B_c} \quad\in\operatorname{Gal}(B_c/\Q). \tag{A.85.2} \] The following two statements are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $\mathfrak o_c((P_v))=1$. \item There is $a\in\Q^\times$ such that the augmented cover $T-c=aY^n$ over $C$, with $Y\ne0$, has points at all places of $\Q$, and every prescribed $P_v$ lifts through its actual forgetful map. \end{enumerate} When these statements hold, $a$ can be chosen as a rational $S$-unit times a product of distinct fresh primes whose Frobenius fixes an old-fibre root tuple at $c$. It can have valuation one at a fresh prime outside any prescribed finite set. Equivalently, the complete test consists of the finitely many equalities \[ \sum_{v\in S\cup\{\infty\}} \operatorname{inv}_v(T(P_v)-c,\chi)=0 \quad \bigl(\chi\in \operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{Gal}(B_c/\Q),\Q/\Z)\bigr). \tag{A.85.3} \] Generators of this finite character group suffice. All local points outside $S$ have zero evaluation in this test. Thus the obstruction depends on finitely many local neighborhoods and cannot be removed by changing only the local points outside $S$.

statement: An explicit ideal-class representative of the one-variable obstruction. Fix a prime $\ell$ and an ordinary pair $(A,B)$ in the scope of A.77, including its dyadic extension. Write $\widehat{K_n^\times}_{\ell}$ for the inverse limit of $K_n^\times/(K_n^\times)^{\ell^j}$. There are explicit norm-compatible completed divisors $\mathfrak d_n$ with norm equal to the divisor of $B$. For odd $\ell$ these are finite-prime divisors; for $\ell=2$ they also retain the signs at all real embeddings. Let $\mathcal D_n$ be the corresponding completed divisor group, and let $\mathcal C_n$ be the $\ell$-primary ordinary ideal class group for odd $\ell$, and the two-primary narrow ideal class group for $\ell=2$. statement: The required splitting primes and one tower with dense correction image. Let $M$ be divisible by $24$, and let $a=3u^8$, $b=-2v^8$, where $u,v$ are positive integers prime to six and $\gcd(a,b)=1$. Fix an odd prime $\ell$ and $k\ge1$ with $N=\ell^k\mid M$. Set \[ K=\Q(a^{1/N}),\quad L=K(\mu_N),\quad \mathcal B=\Q(\mu_M,b^{1/M}),\quad \mathcal R=\Q(\mu_D),\qquad M\mid D. \tag{A.95.1} \] For any $\rho\in\operatorname{Gal}(\mathcal R/\Q)$ fixing $\Q(\mu_M)$, and any finite excluded set of rational primes, the subgroup $C_{\rm split}$ of A.92 is generated by the split-prime difference classes at primes $q$ outside that set which simultaneously satisfy \[ q\text{ splits completely in }L\text{ and }\mathcal B, \qquad \operatorname{Frob}_q|_{\mathcal R}=\rho. \tag{A.95.2} \] In particular a finite set of such primes supplies all the required class generators. There is an ordinary infinite-support pair $(A,B)$ of the two-prime type of A.44, with $v_3(A)=v_2(B)=1$ and $v_2(A)=0$, for which the actual nested $3$-power root tower of A.77 satisfies \[ \varprojlim_r W_r\longrightarrow C_{n_j}^0 \text{ is surjective for every }n_j=v_3((j+4)!). \tag{A.95.3} \] All these maps belong to this one pair and this one tower. Consequently \[ \operatorname{im}\left(\varprojlim_r W_r \longrightarrow\varprojlim_r C_r^0\right) \text{ is dense in }\varprojlim_r C_r^0 \tag{A.95.4} \] for its inverse-limit topology. The construction supplies finite-support compatible divisor representatives for each individual target in (A.95.3). It does not assert that these representatives converge as the target level increases, or that the class family in A.86 belongs to the image in (A.95.4).

statement: Quartic common fields and two-coordinate initialization. For nonzero rational numbers $D_1,\ldots,D_k$, put \[ \mathcal E_4=\Q[Z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,Z_k^{\pm1}] /(Z_i^4-D_i),\qquad K=\Q(\sqrt{D_1},\ldots,\sqrt{D_k}). \tag{A.96.1} \] For every nonempty subset $J\subset\{1,\ldots,k\}$ such that $\prod_{i\in J}D_i$ is a negative rational square, let $r_J>0$ be the rational number determined by $\prod_{i\in J}D_i=-r_J^2$. The largest abelian field contained in every field factor of $\mathcal E_4$ is exactly \[ B_4=K\bigl(\sqrt{2r_J}: \prod_{i\in J}D_i=-r_J^2\bigr). \tag{A.96.2} \] The empty list of additional generators gives $B_4=K$. In particular every common character is quadratic. Now let $a,b\in\Q^\times$, let \[ C:\ aX^4-bY^4=1,\qquad T=aX^4,\qquad c\in\Q\setminus\{0,1\},\qquad D_0=c/a,\quad D_1=(c-1)/b. \tag{A.96.3} \] For every common character $\chi$ of the fibre algebra $\Q[Z_0^{\pm1},Z_1^{\pm1}]/(Z_0^4-D_0,Z_1^4-D_1)$, the cyclic class $(T-c,\chi)$ on $C$ is the restriction of an explicitly computed constant in $\operatorname{Br}(\Q)[2]$. Its evaluation at every ordinary local point with $T\ne c$ is that same constant's local evaluation. Consequently the finite-character test of A.85 always vanishes for two old finite punctures at exponent four. More explicitly, for an everywhere locally soluble old quartic cover with two finite punctures, any new rational puncture, any finite set $S$ of places, and one prescribed ordinary old local point at each $v\in S$ avoiding that puncture admit a rational new coefficient whose augmented quartic cover is everywhere locally soluble and whose forgetful map lifts every prescribed point. This assertion concerns the actual finite initialization problem at exponent four.

statement: Rigidity from the own coefficient and from one global coefficient. Let $A,B\in\widehat{\Q^\times}$ be an ordinary completed unit-equation pair: for every finite prime $p$ there is $x_p\in\Q_p\setminus\{0,1\}$ with \[ A_p=\kappa_p(x_p),\qquad B_p=\kappa_p(1-x_p) \quad\hbox{in }\widehat{\Q_p^\times}. \tag{A.97.1} \] For a coefficient prime $\ell$, put \[ \begin{split} M_\ell&=\varprojlim_n\Q^\times/(\Q^\times)^{\ell^n},\\ M_{p,\ell}&=\varprojlim_n \Q_p^\times/(\Q_p^\times)^{\ell^n}. \end{split} \tag{A.97.2} \] Write $A_\ell\in M_\ell$ for the global coefficient projection and $A_{p,\ell}\in M_{p,\ell}$ for its localization; use the same notation for $B$ and rational numbers. These are the actual continuous homomorphisms induced by $\Q^\times\hookrightarrow\Q_p^\times$ and by restricting the inverse limit to the powers of $\ell$. Fix $\lambda\in\Q\setminus\{0,1\}$. If the own-coefficient equalities \[ A_{p,p}=\lambda_{p,p},\qquad B_{p,p}=(1-\lambda)_{p,p} \tag{A.97.3} \] hold on a set of rational primes of Dirichlet density one, then \[ A=\lambda,\qquad B=1-\lambda, \qquad x_p=\lambda \quad\hbox{for every finite }p. \tag{A.97.4} \] In fact, at any single prime $p$, (A.97.3) already implies $x_p=\lambda$. If (A.97.4) fails, there is a nonempty Chebotarev conjugacy class of primes, apart from finitely many exceptions, at each of which at least one of the two own-coefficient equalities fails. There is also a fixed-global-coefficient criterion. For any one coefficient prime $\ell$, the equalities \[ A_\ell=\lambda_\ell, \qquad B_\ell=(1-\lambda)_\ell \quad\hbox{in }M_\ell \tag{A.97.5} \] imply (A.97.4). Thus an ordinary completed pair cannot be changed from a rational pair only at a proper subset of the global coefficient primes. This includes every finite-primary patching of a rational pair. The density-one assertion requires ordinary local points only at the density-one comparison primes; under that weaker hypothesis its conclusion is the equality of the two full global classes $A=\lambda$, $B=1-\lambda$. Moreover, a noncuspidal Selmer section in A.14's labeled rational realization range, different from its realized point section, differs from that rational point's global Kummer coefficient pair at every prime in some nonempty Chebotarev conjugacy class, apart from finitely many exceptions. In particular no finite-primary or density-zero-primary modification gives such a section. The fixed-global-coefficient assertion (A.97.5) retains the all-place ordinary hypothesis (A.97.1). No local section theorem is used in these statements; ordinariness is the explicit hypothesis (A.97.1).

statement: A non-surjective completed norm-fibre transition at the rational point three. Let $\alpha=3^{1/3}>0$, $\gamma=3^{1/9}>0$, $K=\Q(\alpha)$ and $E=\Q(\gamma)$, with the actual inclusion $K\hookrightarrow E$ given by $\alpha=\gamma^3$. Write $\widehat{F^\times}_3=\varprojlim_r F^\times/(F^\times)^{3^r}$ for each of these fields, and define \[ \mathcal F_F(-2)= \{z\in\widehat{F^\times}_3:\mathrm N_{F/\Q}(z)=\kappa_3(-2)\}. \tag{A.98.1} \] The continuous norm map \[ \mathrm N_{E/K}:\mathcal F_E(-2)\longrightarrow\mathcal F_K(-2) \tag{A.98.2} \] is not surjective, although both fibres are nonempty. An explicit element outside its image is the Kummer class of \[ \begin{aligned} u&=\frac{(4-\alpha)^3}{61},& \beta&=(1-\alpha)u =\frac{25-109\alpha+60\alpha^2}{61},\\ \mathrm N_{K/\Q}(u)&=1,& \mathrm N_{K/\Q}(\beta)&=-2. \end{aligned} \tag{A.98.3} \] More generally, let $Q,R\in\Q^\times$ have zero valuation at $61$, and let $e$ be a positive integer prime to three. For the actual cubic extension \[ E_Q=K(\gamma_Q),\qquad \gamma_Q^3=Q^e\alpha, \tag{A.98.4} \] the completed element $\kappa_3(\beta R^e)$ is not in $\mathrm N_{E_Q/K}(\widehat{E_Q^\times}_3)$. These are exactly the norm-representative transitions associated with the coefficient change $a=3\mapsto3Q^{3e}$ and $b=-2\mapsto-2R^{3e}$. Finally an ordinary local completed pair at $61$ whose second coordinate is congruent to $-2$ modulo cubes cannot have positive first-coordinate valuation there. Thus the prime in this example cannot be converted into positive $A$-support while preserving that second-coordinate cube class.

statement: A ray-class repair inside the actual rational norm fibre. Retain the finite data $a,b,M,\ell,N,K,L,\mathcal B,\mathcal R$ of (A.95.1), with $\ell$ odd, and let $\beta\in K^\times$ satisfy $\mathrm N_{K/\Q}\beta=b$. Fix $r\ge1$ and a finite set $S$ of rational primes containing two, the support of $b$, and every prime ramified in $L/\Q$. Let $\mathfrak m$ be any finite ray modulus of $K$ supported above $S\setminus\{2\}$. Prescribe $\rho\in\operatorname{Gal}(\mathcal R/\Q)$ fixing $\Q(\mu_M)$, as in A.95. Then there is an actual element $\beta'\in K^\times$ and a finite set $Q$ of rational primes, disjoint from $S$ and the support of $\beta$, such that \[ \begin{aligned} \mathrm N_{K/\Q}\beta'&=b,\\ v_{\mathfrak p}(\beta')&=v_{\mathfrak p}(\beta) &&(\mathfrak p\mid S),\\ \beta'/\beta&\equiv1\pmod{\mathfrak m},\\ v_{\mathfrak p}(\beta')&\equiv0\pmod{\ell^r} &&(\mathfrak p\nmid S\cup Q). \end{aligned} \tag{A.99.1} \] Every $q\in Q$ splits completely in both $L$ and $\mathcal B$, and has cyclotomic Frobenius $\rho$ in $\mathcal R$. The set $Q$ may avoid any further prescribed finite set and may lie above any prescribed bound. At each such $q$ the valuation vector of $\beta'$ has ordinary sum zero, so its rational norm contributes no new coefficient prime. This repairs one norm representative at the specified finite precision. For an intermediate field $K_0\subset K$, the proof gives an explicit multiplier $u^{-t}$ and hence the exact additional transition \[ \frac{\mathrm N_{K/K_0}\beta'}{\mathrm N_{K/K_0}\beta} =(\mathrm N_{K/K_0}u)^{-t}. \tag{A.99.2} \] Its rational norm is one. The statement does not assert that (A.99.2) is an $\ell^r$th power in $K_0$, or that separate applications preserve a previously chosen norm chain in the radical tower.

statement: Relative ray-class repair in one existing finite norm chain. Fix the odd-prime data of A.95 with $\ell^t\mid M$, and choose compatible positive roots of the current rational coefficient $a$. For $0\le s<t$ put \[ E=\Q(a^{1/\ell^t}),\qquad K=\Q(a^{1/\ell^s})\subset E,\qquad L=E(\mu_{\ell^t}). \tag{A.100.1} \] Here $K=\Q$ when $s=0$. For the nested fields of A.77 these are the same actual subfields after the explicit rational rescaling of roots in (A.86.1). Let $\beta\in E^\times$ have rational norm $b$, and put $\beta_s=\mathrm N_{E/K}\beta$. Fix a precision $\ell^r$, a finite rational-prime set $S$ containing two, every prime ramified in $L/\Q$, and the rational primes below the support of $\beta_s$. Let $\mathfrak m$ be a finite ray modulus of $E$ supported above $S\setminus\{2\}$. Retain the prescribed cyclotomic Frobenius $\rho$ of A.95. There is $\beta'\in E^\times$ with the same exact rational norm $b$, the same valuations above $S$, and $\beta'/\beta\equiv1\pmod{\mathfrak m}$, such that all valuations outside $S$ and finitely many permitted primes $Q$ are divisible by $\ell^r$. Every $q\in Q$ splits completely in $L$ and the current $B$-radical field, has the prescribed cyclotomic Frobenius, and may avoid any fixed finite set and lie above any fixed bound. At each such $q$, the new valuation vector has sum zero \emph{separately above each prime of $K$ over $q$}. Moreover there is an actual unit $\eta\in\mathcal O_K^\times$ such that \[ \mathrm N_{E/K}\beta' =\beta_s\eta^{\ell^r}. \tag{A.100.2} \] Consequently, for every field $K_i$ in the same chain below $K$, the exact identity \[ \frac{\mathrm N_{E/K_i}\beta'}{\mathrm N_{E/K_i}\beta} =(\mathrm N_{K/K_i}\eta)^{\ell^r} \tag{A.100.3} \] preserves the lower norm class modulo $\ell^r$. This repairs the support of an already existing finite chain. It does not supply a new norm preimage of an arbitrarily fixed lower representative.

statement: The actual permutation Kummer field and its boundary intersections. Let $a=3u^8$, $b=-2v^8$ be the current coefficients of A.44, with $u,v$ prime to six, and let $N=3^n$, $n\ge1$. Put $K=\Q(\alpha)$, $\alpha^N=a$. Let $\beta\in K^\times$ have rational norm $b$ and the following specified divisor above two: valuation one at the unique degree-one prime, and zero at every other prime of $K$ above two. Fix $r\ge1$, an integer $M$ divisible by $\operatorname{lcm}(24,N)$, and a cyclotomic field \[ R=\Q(\mu_D),\qquad \operatorname{lcm}(M,3^r)\mid D. \tag{A.101.1} \] Write $L_R=R(\alpha)$ and let $\tau(\alpha)=\zeta_N\alpha$, $\tau|_R=1$. For $i\in\Z/N\Z$ put $\beta_i=\tau^i\beta$, and choose $\delta_i^{3^r}=\beta_i$. Define the actual splitting fields \[ S_\beta=L_R(\delta_i:i\in\Z/N\Z),\qquad B_R=R(b^{1/M}),\qquad S=S_\beta B_R. \tag{A.101.2} \] Then \[ \operatorname{Gal}(S_\beta/R) =(\Z/3^r\Z)^N\rtimes\Z/N\Z \tag{A.101.3} \] with the literal cyclic permutation action, and with the explicit splitting on the displayed generators given below. Its maximal abelian subfield over $R$ is \[ (S_\beta)^{\rm ab/R} =R(\alpha,\delta_*),\qquad \delta_*=\prod_i\delta_i,\qquad \delta_*^{3^r}=b. \tag{A.101.4} \] Put $m=v_3(M)$ and $d=\min(r,m)$. The exact boundary intersection is \[ S_\beta\cap B_R=R(b^{1/3^d}). \tag{A.101.5} \] Both $S_\beta$ and the simultaneous field $S$ have maximal abelian subfield over $\Q$ exactly $R$. The assertion for $S$ follows from the full simultaneous group computation below, including its common $b$-subfield. Let $F$ be the compositum of $L=\Q(\alpha,\mu_N)$ with the conjugates of a three-primary ray class field of $K$ whose modulus excludes two, as in A.99. Then \[ FR\cap S=L_R. \tag{A.101.6} \] Consequently the permitted split primes generating the class targets in A.95 and A.100 may additionally split every conjugate radical in $S_\beta$. Any larger cyclotomic CRT automorphism fixing $R$ can be retained. In particular, if $v_3(D)=r\ge v_3(M)$, the additional condition $v_3(q-1)=r$ is available by prescribing the nontrivial class $1+3^r$ modulo $3^{r+1}$.

statement: All bad-place comparisons can hold while a good place obstructs the quotient section. Put $\lambda=254$, let $s_\lambda$ be its rational point section, and write \[ C_H=\ker(\Pi\longrightarrow H),\qquad \mathcal Q=E_U/(C_H\cap\Gamma_2\Pi). \tag{A.102.1} \] There is an explicit continuous section $\sigma:G_\Q\to\mathcal Q$ with the following properties. Its projection to $E_H$ is literally the projection of $s_\lambda$. Its completed Kummer coordinates have finite support contained in $\{2,11,23,127\}$ and are different from $(254,-253)$. At the four bad primes of $E_{254}$ its local section classes in this same quotient are as follows: \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{physical prime}&\text{actual local source of the quotient section}\\ \hline 2,11&\text{the point }254\\ 127&\text{a full local cusp-0 section}\\ 23&\text{a full local cusp-1 section}. \end{array} \tag{A.102.2} \] These are simultaneous comparisons in $\mathcal Q$, with geometric conjugators, rather than separate comparisons in its two factors. The Tate comparisons preserve the integral Weil pairings. At the good prime $47$, the section is the image of neither an ordinary point nor any of the three cusp packets. The obstruction is already visible in the finite geometric abelian quotient at exponent $46$. Consequently $\sigma$ is not the image of a Selmer section of $E_U$. No lift to a full section is constructed. This gives an exact example in which the global full-$H$ comparison, finite Kummer support, and every bad-place point or cusp comparison all hold, while a good-place comparison fails. Moreover, every noncuspidal Selmer section in A.14 with arbitrary labeled integral realization $E_{254}$ is $s_{254}$. The proof uses the forced coefficient-$23$ data from the surviving bad-place configuration in the residue field at $47$. This conclusion requires no full-$H$ hypothesis on that section.

statement: The coupled residue equations survive boundary and prior-radical splitting. Let $K=\Q(\alpha)$, $\alpha^3=3$, and put \[ \begin{gathered} q=22441,\qquad c=4048,\qquad H=c^3-3=q\cdot2955829,\\ \beta_0=1-\alpha,\qquad u=\frac{(c-\alpha)^3}{H},\qquad \beta=\beta_0u. \end{gathered} \tag{A.103.1} \] Then $N_{K/\Q}u=1$ and $N_{K/\Q}\beta=-2$. For every integer $e$ prime to three, every $Q\in\Q^\times$, and every $R\in\Q^\times$ with $v_q(R)=0$, the actual cubic extension \[ E_Q=K(\gamma),\qquad \gamma^3=Q^e\alpha \tag{A.103.3} \] has the following property: $\beta R^e$ is not a norm from $E_Q^\times$ to $K^\times$. It is not a norm between their three-primary completions either. There is no restriction on $k=v_q(Q)$; in particular allocating $q$ to the updated $A$-coefficient does not repair this specified representative. statement: The four simultaneous projection classes and their detection at three. Fix $\lambda\in\Q\setminus\{0,1\}$ and its point section $s_\lambda$. Put \[ \begin{split} C_H&=\ker(\Pi\longrightarrow H),\qquad E_J=E_U/(C_H\cap\Gamma_2\Pi),\\ T&=\Pi^{\rm ab}=\widehat\Z(1)^2,\qquad M=H^{\rm ab},\qquad K=\ker(T\longrightarrow M). \end{split} \tag{A.104.1} \] For $k=\Q$ or $\Q_3$, let $\mathcal F_k(\lambda)$ be the set of geometric conjugacy classes of continuous sections of $(E_J)_k\to G_k$ whose projections to $(E_H)_k$ and $(E_1)_k$ have the same geometric conjugacy classes as the respective projections of $s_\lambda$. Here $E_1=E_U/\Gamma_2\Pi$, and the local extensions are the pullbacks along the chosen map $G_{\Q_3}\to G_\Q$. Both sets have exactly four elements. Relative to the point splitting they have the exact description \[ \mathcal F_k(\lambda) \simeq M^{G_k} =\{(4\epsilon_0,4\epsilon_1,0): \epsilon_0,\epsilon_1\in\{0,1\}\}, \tag{A.104.2} \] using A.56's coordinates $M=(\Z/8(1))^2\oplus\Z/3(1)$. Restriction from $\Q$ to $\Q_3$ is a bijection between these four-element sets, identified with the identity on (A.104.2). Only the zero element has the local class of an ordinary point or cusp at three. For $E_\lambda$ good at three, the three nonzero classes already have no ordinary or cuspidal source in the explicit geometric quotient \[ J_{32,16}= (H_2\bmod32) \mathbin{\times}_{(\Z/8(1))^2} (\Z/16(1))^2, \qquad |J_{32,16}|=8192. \tag{A.104.3} \] The arithmetic quotient uses the action induced by $s_\lambda$; the displayed fibre product and its map from $\Pi$ are the ones induced by A.56. This includes every rational Legendre parameter with $j=1728$. If $E_\lambda$ is potentially multiplicative at three, put $e=-v_3(j(E_\lambda))/2$ and $N=5+v_2(e)$. Replacing $H_2\bmod32$ in (A.104.3) by $H_2\bmod2^N$ gives an explicit quotient of order $2^{3N-2}$ that distinguishes the four local classes from one another. Thus the two projection classes by themselves admit three additional quotient classes, with exact relative-sign parameters (A.104.2), but none of the additional classes matches locally at three. The statement classifies this specified simultaneous projection fibre, not the whole fibre over the $H$ projection alone. No local section theorem is used.

statement: Actual finite norm-one classes, approximation, and the auxiliary local condition. Let $a\in\Q^\times$ have $v_3(a)=1$, let $N=3^n$ with $n\ge1$, and put $K=\Q(\alpha)$, $\alpha^N=a$. For $r\ge1$ write \[ R_r=\Z/3^r\Z,\qquad d=\max(n,r),\qquad L=\Q(\alpha,\mu_{3^d}),\qquad G=C_N\rtimes U_d,\quad U_d=(\Z/3^d\Z)^\times. \tag{A.109.1} \] The displayed group is the actual group $\operatorname{Gal}(L/\Q)$. Let $H=U_d$ be the stabilizer of $\alpha$, and define \[ P_r=R_r[G/H],\quad I_r=\ker(P_r\xrightarrow{\sum}R_r), \quad J_r=P_r/R_r\mathbf1, \quad T=\ker\bigl(\operatorname{Res}_{K/\Q}\mathbf G_m \xrightarrow{N}\mathbf G_m\bigr). \tag{A.109.2} \] There are canonical identifications of finite $G_\Q$-modules \[ M_r:=T[3^r]=I_r\otimes\mu_{3^r},\qquad M_r^\vee:=\operatorname{Hom}(M_r,\mu_{3^r})=J_r. \tag{A.109.3} \] Both $H^1(G,M_r)$ and $H^1(G,J_r)$ vanish. For either $C=M_r$ or $C=J_r$ and every finite set $S$ of places, the actual localization map \[ H^1(\Q,C)\longrightarrow\prod_{v\in S}H^1(\Q_v,C) \tag{A.109.4} \] is onto. Every nonzero global class has nonzero restriction to $G_L$ and is detected at infinitely many primes splitting completely in $L$. This last assertion allows exclusion of a fixed finite set of primes. The classes represented by actual global norm-one elements are exactly \[ \operatorname{im}\bigl(T(\Q)/T(\Q)^{3^r}\to H^1(\Q,M_r)\bigr) =\left\{c:\operatorname{loc}_v(c)\in \operatorname{im}\bigl(T(\Q_v)/T(\Q_v)^{3^r}\bigr) \text{ for every }v\right\}. \tag{A.109.5} \] At a prime $q\ne3$ splitting completely in $L$, choose compatible local Kummer coordinates. Then \[ H^1(\Q_q,M_r)=I_r\oplus I_r,\qquad H^1(\Q_q,J_r)=J_r\oplus J_r, \tag{A.109.6} \] where $(t,c)$ records tame inertia and Frobenius, respectively. For $z\in R_r$ the graph $\mathcal L_z=\{(t,zt):t\in I_r\}$ consists exactly of the classes whose local image is generated by its tame inertia image and whose chosen Frobenius equals $z$ times that inertia generator. Its Tate orthogonal is the graph $\{(u,zu):u\in J_r\}$. At precision three, every ramified class with cyclic local image lies on one of these graphs. The unramified classes form the separate subspace $\{(0,c)\}$. Here is the direct map to the next norm equation. Suppose additionally that $q$ splits the next pure-radical field, so all conjugates $\alpha_i$ are cubes in $\Q_q$, and that $q$ is prime to the target rational norm $b$, with $b$ a local cube. Write the local coordinates of an actual target $\beta$ of norm $b$ as $t_i=v_q(\beta_i)\bmod3$ and $c_i=[q^{-v_q(\beta_i)}\beta_i]$ in the unit cubic quotient. For $Q=q^kQ_0$, $R$ a $q$-unit, and $3\nmid ek$, the simultaneous local conditions \[ \beta_iR^e\in N_{\Q_q((Q^e\alpha_i)^{1/3})/\Q_q} \Q_q((Q^e\alpha_i)^{1/3})^\times \quad\text{for every }i \tag{A.109.7} \] are exactly \[ c=z t+w\mathbf1,\qquad z=[Q_0]/k,\qquad w=-e[R]\quad\text{in }\F_3. \tag{A.109.8} \] Thus a locally cubic $R$ gives the graph condition itself. No assertion of unrestricted approximation with (A.109.8) at all new ramification is made; A.110 gives an explicit obstruction to it.

statement: The complete finite pairing spaces and simultaneous correction at three. Let $a\in\Q^\times$ have $v_3(a)=1$, let $n\in\{2,3\}$, and put \[ N=3^n,\qquad d=N/3,\qquad K_n=\Q(\alpha),\quad \alpha^N=a,\qquad K_{n-1}=\Q(\alpha^3),\qquad L_n=K_n(\mu_N). \tag{A.113.1} \] The relative norm-one torus and its actual three-torsion module are \[ \begin{gathered} T_n^{\rm rel}=\ker\bigl(\operatorname{Res}_{K_n/\Q}\mathbf G_m \xrightarrow{N}\operatorname{Res}_{K_{n-1}/\Q}\mathbf G_m\bigr),\\ M_n^{\rm rel}=T_n^{\rm rel}[3] =\ker(P_N\longrightarrow P_d)\otimes\mu_3, \end{gathered} \tag{A.113.2} \] where $P_b=\F_3[\Z/b\Z]$ and the displayed map sums coordinates congruent modulo $d$. Let $G=\operatorname{Gal}(L_n/\Q)=C_N\rtimes(\Z/N\Z)^\times$. Then \[ \dim_{\F_3}\operatorname{Hom}_G (\mathop{\bigwedge}\nolimits^2M_n^{\rm rel},\mu_3)=n. \tag{A.113.3} \] Here is an explicit basis of this entire space. Write $\F_3[C_N]=\F_3[Z]/(Z^N)$, with $Z=x-1$, so that $M_n^{\rm rel}=Z^d\F_3[Z]/(Z^N)\otimes\mu_3$. On each block of three coordinates use its sum-zero relation and set \[ \mathcal B_*(v,w)=\sum_{h=0}^{d-1} (v_hw_{h+d}-v_{h+d}w_h), \qquad z=\frac{Z^2}{1+Z}. \tag{A.113.4} \] The expression is a $G$-equivariant nondegenerate alternating form with values in $\mu_3$. For $0\le j<n$ put \[ \mathcal B_j(v,w)=\mathcal B_*(v,z^{\,d-3^j}w). \tag{A.113.5} \] These are the promised basis, with \[ \operatorname{rank}\mathcal B_j=2\cdot3^j,\qquad \operatorname{rad}\mathcal B_j =Z^{d+2\cdot3^j}\F_3[Z]/(Z^N)\otimes\mu_3. \tag{A.113.6} \] The projective ranks are respectively $\{6:3,\ 2:1\}$ for $n=2$, and $\{18:9,\ 6:3,\ 2:1\}$ for $n=3$, where each value after a colon is the number of projective forms of that rank. Identify $\tfrac13\Z/\Z$ with $\F_3$. The simultaneous, explicitly defined local map \[ \begin{split} T_n^{\rm rel}(\Q_3)/T_n^{\rm rel}(\Q_3)^3 &\longrightarrow\F_3^n,\\ u&\longmapsto \left(\operatorname{inv}_3\left( \tfrac12(\mathcal B_j)_* (\kappa_T(u)\smile\kappa_T(u))\right)\right)_{j=0}^{n-1} \end{split} \tag{A.113.7} \] is onto. Consequently every collection of the quadratic reciprocity values obtained from equivariant alternating forms on this precise relative module can be compensated at three, when that local multiplier is free. This assertion supplies the local map (A.113.7); it does not construct a global multiplier with prescribed new ramification.

statement: Quadratic-coset Kummer detection and the cubic source fibre. Let $D\in\Q^\times/\Q^{\times2}$ be nontrivial, let $K_D=\Q(\sqrt D)$, and let $\mathcal P_D$ be its unramified nonsplit rational primes. Put $M_\ell=\varprojlim_n\Q^\times/\Q^{\times\ell^n}$, embedded in $\widehat{\Q^\times}$ by the primary product map of A.97. Define the following set of coefficient primes: \[ \mathcal E_D=\{\ell:K_D\subset\Q(\mu_{\ell^\infty})\}. \tag{A.114.1} \] It is empty or a singleton. Its nonempty cases, with $D$ represented by a squarefree integer, are \[ \begin{array}{c|c} D&\mathcal E_D\\ \hline -1,\ 2,\ -2&\{2\}\\ (-1)^{(\ell-1)/2}\ell,\quad\ell\text{ odd prime}&\{\ell\}. \end{array} \tag{A.114.2} \] If a completed class $C$ is trivial in $\widehat{\Q_p^\times}$ at every prime of $\mathcal P_D$, or at all but finitely many of them, then every primary component of $C$ outside $\mathcal E_D$ is zero. In particular this localization is injective when $\mathcal E_D$ is empty. The possible single primary component cannot be removed from this assertion in general. statement: Exact recursion and stabilization of the common dyadic fields. Fix $D_1,\ldots,D_k\in\Q^\times$ and write \[ D_i=(-1)^{\delta_i}\prod_{P\in\mathcal P}P^{w_{iP}}, \qquad \delta_i\in\{0,1\},\quad W=(w_{iP}). \tag{A.126.1} \] For each $n=2^r$, $r\ge1$, let $B_n$ be the largest abelian extension of $\Q$ contained in every field factor of \[ \mathcal E_n=\Q[Z_i^{\pm1}:1\le i\le k]/(Z_i^n-D_i)_i. \tag{A.126.2} \] The square-coordinate maps give actual inclusions $B_{n/2}\subset B_n$, and $B_2=\Q(\sqrt{D_i}:1\le i\le k)$. For $n\ge4$ the following recursion computes the entire field. When $\mu_n$ is not contained in $B_{n/2}$, one has \[ B_{2^s}=B_{n/2}\qquad(2^s\ge n). \tag{A.126.3} \] When $\mu_n\subset B_{n/2}$, put $m=n/2$ and define \[ \begin{gathered} \mathcal R_m=\ker\bigl(W^{\mathsf t}:(\Z/m)^k \longrightarrow(\Z/m)^{\mathcal P}\bigr),\\ 0\le t_i<m,\qquad r_t=\prod_P P^{\frac1m\sum_i t_iw_{iP}}>0, \qquad \delta_t=\sum_i t_i\delta_i\pmod2,\\ \prod_iD_i^{t_i}=(-1)^{\delta_t}r_t^m. \end{gathered} \tag{A.126.4} \] Let $\chi_{2n}$ be the even character of $(\Z/2n)^\times=\langle-1\rangle\times\langle5\rangle$ with $\chi_{2n}(5)=1/m$. For each relation set \[ \lambda_t=\chi_{r_t}+\delta_t\chi_{2n}, \qquad K_t=\overline\Q^{\ker\lambda_t}. \tag{A.126.5} \] Here $\chi_{r_t}$ is the quadratic character of $r_t$; a trivial character defines $K_t=\Q$. Then \[ B_n=B_{n/2}(K_t:t\in\mathcal R_m). \tag{A.126.6} \] Every displayed field is included in every actual factor by the root maps in the proof. The relative extension $B_n/B_{n/2}$ is elementary abelian of exponent two. There is also an exact alternative for the infinite tower. An integral vector $t$ with \[ W^{\mathsf t}t=0,\qquad \sum_i\delta_i t_i=1\pmod2 \tag{A.126.7} \] gives $\prod_iD_i^{t_i}=-1$ and forces $\Q(\mu_{2n})\subset B_n$ for every dyadic $n$. In the absence of such a vector, let $d_1,\ldots,d_\rho$ be the nonzero integral Smith invariants of $W^{\mathsf t}$, and set \[ a=\max_j v_2(d_j),\qquad a=0\text{ when }\rho=0. \tag{A.126.8} \] The tower is then constant for every $n\ge2^{a+2}$. For $a=0$ it is already constantly $B_2$. Thus (A.126.7) decides exactly whether this common-field tower is unbounded. For any odd positive integer $v$ and any dyadic $n\ge4$, the same radicands also satisfy \[ B_{nv}=B_n. \tag{A.126.21} \] Here $B_{nv}$ is defined by (A.126.2) with exponent $nv$; the equality uses the actual map $z_i\mapsto z_i^v$. statement: The semi-invariant operator module and its exact coefficient maps. Let \(a\in\Q^\times\) satisfy \(v_3(a)=1\), let \(n,r\ge1\), and retain the actual relative norm torus \(T_n\) of A.115. Put \[ N=3^n,\quad d=N/3,\quad R_r=\Z/3^r\Z,\quad C_r=T_n[3^r],\quad m=\max(n,r). \tag{A.129.1} \] Use compatible roots of unity to write the actual splitting group as \(G_{n,r}=C_N\rtimes U_m\), with \(U_m=(\Z/3^m\Z)^\times\). Let \(\rho_r:C_r\to C_1\) be multiplication by \(3^{r-1}\), and let \(\iota_r:\mu_3\hookrightarrow\mu_{3^r}\) be inclusion. Every equivariant bilinear form is alternating, and the map \[ \begin{split} \operatorname{Hom}_{G_\Q}(\textstyle\bigwedge^2 C_1,\mu_3) &\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \operatorname{Hom}_{G_\Q}(C_r\otimes_{R_r}C_r,\mu_{3^r}),\\ B&\longmapsto\iota_r\circ B\circ(\rho_r,\rho_r) \end{split} \tag{A.129.2} \] is an isomorphism of abelian groups. In particular the group on the right is \((\Z/3\Z)^n\), and every form has values in the literal order-three subgroup of \(\mu_{3^r}\). Here is the integral operator calculation giving the map. Put \[ \mathcal O_n=\Z_3[x]/(\Phi_N(x)),\qquad \Phi_N(x)=1+x^d+x^{2d},\qquad \sigma_u(x)=x^u. \tag{A.129.3} \] Let \(\omega(u)\in\{1,-1\}\) lift \(u\bmod3\), and let \(\chi_r(u)=u\bmod3^r\). Under the perfect underlying block pairing of A.115, the group of forms in (A.129.2) is exactly \[ \begin{split} \{P\in\mathcal O_n/3^r:\ \sigma_u(P)=\omega(u)\chi_r(u)P\text{ for all }u\in U_m\} &=\ker(\sigma_2+2:\mathcal O_n/3^r\to\mathcal O_n/3^r)\\ &=3^{r-1}\ker(\sigma_2-1:\mathcal O_n/3\to\mathcal O_n/3). \end{split} \tag{A.129.4} \] The last notation means the image of the kernel under \(\mathcal O_n/3\to\mathcal O_n/3^r\), \(P\mapsto3^{r-1}\widetilde P\). It is independent of the chosen lift. The coefficient transitions retain their literal maps. For \(r\ge2\), reducing the value of any such form by \(\mu_{3^r}\xrightarrow{z\mapsto z^3}\mu_{3^{r-1}}\) gives zero. Restricting its two arguments to the subgroup \(C_{r-1}\hookrightarrow C_r\) also gives zero. For an actual continuous class \(\gamma\in H^1(\Q_v,C_r)\), the associated quadratic class is \[ \tfrac12\bigl(\iota_r B(\rho_r,\rho_r)\bigr)_* (\gamma\cup\gamma) =(\iota_r)_*\!\left( \tfrac12 B_*((\rho_r)_*\gamma\cup(\rho_r)_*\gamma)\right). \tag{A.129.5} \] Consequently these higher-precision bilinear reciprocity tests are exactly the mod-three tests under the displayed maps. They do not characterize a higher-precision local cyclic image: an explicit relative norm-one class at precision nine below has every displayed bilinear value zero and has noncyclic local image.

Define \[ \begin{split} \mathcal H_r&=\bigcup_{\substack{P\subset{ m cs}(E)\setminus S\\ P\ {\rm finite}}} H^1(G_{\Q,S\cup P},C),\\ \mathcal H_{r,\rm cyc}&=\{\gamma\in\mathcal H_r: \operatorname{res}_p\gamma\text{ has cyclic image at every} \ p\notin S\text{ where it ramifies}\}. \end{split} \tag{A.130.2} \] Every such ramified prime splits the coefficient field, so the local image is that of an actual homomorphism into \(C\). In particular, arbitrary prescriptions at finitely many split-\(E\) primes, with zero prescribed at the other controlled places, have such a lift exactly when their total values (A.130.3) vanish. Pure tame prescriptions always have this property. statement: All-place finite matching gives a unique completed coordinate. Every finite class \([a_N]\) is unique, and their reductions are automatically compatible. Thus there is no further inverse-limit obstruction after the all-place finite matching in (A.132.2). If no real sign is prescribed, project the equality to the finite places; all-place finite matching then determines the one possible global sign. There is also the exact character description of the same image. statement: The precise local and adelic consequences of a birational lift. Let $k$ be a number field and $X/k$ a hyperbolic curve with smooth completion $\overline X$. A section in $\Sec^{\mathrm{bir}}(X/k)$ is locally a point or cusp section. At finite places this supplies centers $x_v\in\overline X(k_v)$; at real places the section specifies a connected component. Such a section is either globally cuspidal or is integral on $X$ at a set of finite places of Dirichlet density one. A birationally adelic section means one admitting a single birational lift whose image on every nonempty open $V\subseteq X$ is adelic on $V$ or cuspidal. Here adelic requires ordinary local sections everywhere and integrality at all but finitely many finite places. Over a totally real or imaginary quadratic number field, every noncuspidal birationally adelic section is a rational point section. In particular, every adelic section of the tripod over $\Q$ is a rational point section.
